# Selected event publication sites and stored Mu child contexts

Checked: 2026-10-19. Proof checkpoint: `8a62bd5e7`.
Verified start: `4486d9ce6`. Source main: `184bba662`.
Evidence: `restart-evidence/20261019-recursive-event-publications/`.

This checkpoint retains the same captured event publication history at a
selected recursive observation. It also derives supported child calls for
literal rows returned by actual stored Mu unfolding. Neither result
identifies the stored body with the current native compiler callback.

## Actual selected observation prefix

`SourceCurrentRecursiveEntryPublication.entry` starts from the existing
selected Entry and its initial semantic, cost, availability and guard
support. It derives a supported Observation, its path split, both existing
Keeps intervals, and a physical publication History from the outer Project
entry to that observation's entry. Root and Head cases use the literal
initial heap. An ordinary case composes the actual ProjectRows prefix
with the selected child's recursive prefix.

No publication history is inferred across the outer reader Keeps gap.
The producer needs no physical History premise for that gap. It does not
derive an observation-to-readAfter publication interval through that gap.

`SourceCurrentRecursiveEntryPublicationSites.Site` adds a selected site
relation. Root and Head constructors retain their literal entry heaps.
The ordinary constructor follows a selected site of the actual child
Entry and projection frame. Its `entry` producer derives one observation,
its publication prefix, and Site at that same observation.before.

Entry is a proposition. Proof irrelevance does not give unique projection
frames or a unique site for every proof of that proposition. A concrete
site equality needs actual value and frame data and graph determinism.
This checkpoint contains no universal site-uniqueness theorem.

## The same event and exact row path

`SourceCurrentRecursiveEventPublications.fold` keeps the original false
gate, actual Required preparation, actual class FoldReads and the stated
support. A nonplain selected row has an ordinary Route in the final value
or the recursive event alternative.

That alternative retains the actual selected Entry, its event occurrence,
the exact literal residual path, and a supported remaining Observation.
The same Observation retains Site and the event's stronger Source receipt.
The actual ordinary prefix extends that Source with both Keeps and its
publication History. Its captured eventHeap is unchanged. Native or Head
execution receipts remain at that eventHeap.

The full row PathOrigin is derived at observation.readAfter. The literal
event occurrence prepends its residual path. This physical view can differ
from the captured checked native reader. No native memo History is assigned
to the later physical view. The producer does not create a projection of
the unchanged whole event.

The caller still supplies publication History from sourceHeap to the
class-fold entry. An empty-to-sourceHeap prefix or sourceHeap equal to
empty permits an empty-start history at the captured event heap. The full
outer startup and scan chronology remains outside this endpoint.

## Supported literal stored-Mu children

`SourceCurrentStoredMuUnfoldChildContexts.Child` retains an original RowAt
in the stored source body. The output row retains the original symbol,
constraint, arity and selected original child index. The original child
has strictly smaller sizeOf than that stored body.

The returned child is either that exact original child, or it has an
actual lexical execute call at derived current and next heaps. The call
entry retains SemanticHeap, Available for the original child and
Replacements for its lexical map. Actual prefix and suffix operations
supply Grows and issued-name extension on both sides of that call.
No size bound is placed on the generated child.

`unfold_child` consumes an actual unfold of the selected stored Mu,
initial semantic and Mu availability, a literal row of its returned
value, and the selected child. A supplied empty-start physical History
at the reader and actual final growth derive the stored Mu's publication
writer. The original-source induction derives Child. It follows original
union members and nested stored Mu bodies. Their lexical scopes remain
explicit. A local ordinary reference cannot supply a literal row.

This endpoint needs no initial Ready or issued-allocation Path. Its
History supplies no writer-to-reader issued-name extension for arbitrary
historical captures. It does not derive ancestry in the current native
requester's input syntax.

LiteralRootParts.Row traverses ordinary rows and unions. It does not
traverse a retained Mu. An epsilon Origin that needs another Mu unfolding
is therefore outside this child theorem. Do not replace that Origin with
an unproved literal-row premise.

## Constructed checks and verification

The changed-child check builds the closed source
`mu x. outer[mu y. inner[x,y]]`. Both binders use their local references.
Actual outer unfolding returns a different used nested Mu child. The
original stored body has one source row. Every identity child alternative
is excluded. The new producer therefore supplies the exact nonidentity
lexical execute and its semantic, availability, replacement and growth
facts. Its original child has strict smaller sizeOf than the stored body.
This check passes strict and complete proof and axiom checks.

The non-root check builds two ordinary branches with distinct used Mu
children. Both have a nested used binder. The first child call publishes
a new nested Mu. Its key is absent from the initial heap and present
after that call. The selected second child starts at that exact heap.
The stronger Entry producer supplies one Observation, Site and publication
prefix together. Actual two-row data and project determinism prove that
same observation's entry equals the first child's return heap. Its path
is the remaining [0]. The selected new key then derives both local and
empty-start writer receipts from that prefix. The check keeps actual
source index 1, operand index 1 and internal row index 0. It passes strict
and complete proof and axiom checks. Its rows are plain. It asserts no
completed nonplain class fold or full outer scan chronology.

All six production public declarations pass complete statement, proof
and standard-axiom checks. All eight printer settings are retained.
Omitted proof text and nonstandard axioms are rejected. All four selected
production strict logs and both constructed strict logs are empty.
Earlier attempts remain unchanged.

The root personally observed the full default build handle terminate
with exit code zero. It passes 3472 jobs and 73953 axiom checks.
Its sole warning remains the earlier unused inputs at
`InternedFreshOrdinaryClosedCompletion:24:5`.
Heavy jobs use 4294967296 bytes for memory.max and memory.high,
zero memory.swap.max, and a five-minute job cap.

## Remaining work

The next case follows actual selected epsilon expansions through further
Mu values and lexical backedges. It must retain the selected stored source,
binding environment and exact observation. Physical publication History
does not imply an issued allocation Path. Replaying every historical
lexical capture needs stronger actual suffix data or a proof for only
the selected names.

Global source binding ancestry and a recursive renewal bound remain open.
General active-owner exclusion, outer completion, repeated-pass convergence
and concrete Haskell correspondence remain open. The conditional root
language theorem is unchanged. The full-library objective remains active.

All 268 Haskell files and all 207 active package files retain their bytes.
No Haskell defect, local repair or Haskell validation result is added.
FINDINGS keeps every repair entry first for external work. The upstream
ordered, template, subsumption and adapter paths still need refinement
proofs. Publication awaits direct approval. No push or board write occurs.

In simple technical English: fresh construction always finishes in the
Lean model. Under the stated guard conditions, its result represents
exactly the finite trees specified by its expression. A completed supported
modeled root reduction with empty inherited constraints preserves that
exact language.
The root theorem derives the logical startup cache and guard facts.
Field allocation, validity, guard coverage and numeric resources remain
explicit. General termination and Haskell correspondence remain open.

Selected recursive event observations now retain their actual entry Site,
publication prefix and exact row/path origin under the original false gate
and stated preparation and fold support. Literal stored-Mu unfold rows
retain supported calls for their indexed original children. Further epsilon
Mu observations and lexical backedges remain outside that child theorem.
These are ancestry prerequisites. They do not prove a global renewal bound.
